title: Trigonometry
overview: Use compound and double-angle identities and the R sin(x+α) form to solve harder trig equations and find max/min values. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use sec, cosec and cot and their identities and graphs.
Use compound-angle and double-angle identities to simplify expressions and solve equations.
Express a sin θ + b cos θ as R sin(θ+α) or R cos(θ−α).
Find exact values, solutions in a stated interval, and maximum/minimum values.

definitions.definition: cot θ = cos θ/sin θ = 1/tan θ.
An angle written as A±B so its sine, cosine or tangent can be expanded.
A single shifted sine or cosine equal to a linear combination of sin θ and cos θ.

sections.title: Reciprocal functions and identities
content: Know sec²θ=1+tan²θ and cosec²θ=1+cot²θ. Domain exclusions occur wherever the denominator is zero. Sketching the reciprocal graphs helps determine asymptotes, periods and all solutions.
bullets: sec and cosec have range y≤−1 or y≥1.
cot θ has period π radians.

sections.title: Compound and double angles
content: Use sin(A±B)=sin A cos B±cos A sin B and cos(A±B)=cos A cos B∓sin A sin B. From these derive sin2A=2sinAcosA and the three useful forms of cos2A.
bullets: Choose cos2A=1−2sin²A or 2cos²A−1 to eliminate the unwanted function.

sections.title: The R-form
content: For a sinθ+b cosθ=R sin(θ+α), compare coefficients: Rcosα=a and Rsinα=b, so R=√(a²+b²). The interval/quadrant for α must match both signs. The form makes extrema and equations easier.
bullets: Maximum is R and minimum is −R before any vertical shift.
Use a sketch to decide which inverse-trig solution is appropriate.

sections.title: Solving trigonometric equations
content: Reduce to one trig function or R-form, solve the basic equation, then generate every solution in the requested interval. Work in radians unless degrees are stated. Check any values lost by dividing by sinθ or cosθ.
bullets: Write the general symmetry pattern before filtering the interval.
Do not cancel a trig factor unless its zero case has been considered.

examTips: Keep the calculator in the angle mode used by the question.
List solutions in increasing order and include endpoints only when they satisfy the equation.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using the wrong sign in the cosine compound-angle formula.
Finding one inverse-trig value but not the other solutions in the interval.
Choosing α without checking the signs of sin α and cos α.

quickRecall.question: How do you find R in a sinθ+b cosθ?
Why must divided trig factors be checked separately?
quickRecall.answer: A factor may be zero, and dividing by it would discard valid solutions.

quickRecall.question: What is the range of R sin(θ+α)+c?
